title: The Sir Jack Files #13: The Case of the Table of Contents
summary: Meta's Muse built each shared-chat link from the conversation's title. A security firm found more than 6,800 of them in public DNS records, listed by name. Meta paused sharing. What happened, and three habits before you share any AI chat.
transcript: Case thirteen. You share an AI chat with one friend. You don't expect it to turn up in a list anyone can read. Muse is Meta's new AI assistant. Ten million US downloads in forty days. Like many chatbots, it lets you share a conversation as a link. But each link was built from the conversation's title, on a Meta web address. October eighteenth. The security firm Claroc checks passive DNS: public records of the web addresses that computers have looked up. It finds more than six thousand eight hundred Muse share links. Listed by name, like a table of contents. Inside some of them: prep for a meeting with a frontier AI lab. A small-business loan application. A bank fraud alert with partial account details. On October twentieth, Meta paused sharing while it reviews the report. Claroc says it found no sign of misuse. Before you share any AI chat: read the title, strip out names and numbers, and treat every link as public. Case closed.
credits: Noir illustrations drawn in code by AI Broadsheet; figures are anonymous silhouettes, not the people in the story. Narration, sound effects and music generated with ElevenLabs.
